paragraphs: Scala 2.13 (retronym/scala#139): the latest scripted run passed against Zinc b6c94565 and a 2.13.19 snapshot of the scala2-sbt-bridge: 198 scenarios passed, 20 pending (the ones Zinc itself marks pending) and 3 skipped. Two skips are the 2.12-only `-Xmax-classfile-name` scenarios. The third, `module-inheritance-extra-hash`, is a real gap: the bridge side of zinc#1807 is missing, which is the change retronym/scala#135 is porting as a draft.

Scala 3 (retronym/scala3#26): the latest run that reached the tests passed with 169 scenarios, 18 pending and 34 skipped. Five skips are reasoned as Scala 3 bridge gaps: `constructors-unrelated-2` (zinc#1324), `module-inheritance-extra-hash` (zinc#1807, the same symptom as on 2.13), `empty-package`, `malformed-class-name-with-dollar` and `main-discovery`. Thirteen are Scala 2 only scenarios, two are pending in Zinc but pass on Scala 3, and fourteen are not triaged yet, most of them because `run` finds no main class. The newest push to that branch is red, but it stopped at the publish step in under a minute, before any test ran, so the last scripted result is still the green one.

What this says about porting: of the five zinc fixes that have scripted tests, #1324 and #1807 reproduce on Scala 3 and look like real ports. #1782 passes, though I haven't checked that its scenarios exercise the Scala 3 path. #1803 can't be judged until its scenario is rewritten with `&` instead of `with`, and #1507's scenario names an explicit 2.13.x label so it doesn't run on Scala 3 at all. So the answer to "do we need an 11287 for Scala 3?" is a small set of fixes, not a wholesale port, with two of the five still unknown.

Zinc itself has 3 disabled scenarios (`binary-3`, `canon`, `inline`) and 20 pending, none with a recorded reason. `inline` is the scenario for zinc#1310, the one confirmed port gap on 2.13, so no CI run anywhere exercises it today.
